messages.author: 224a7d15b7a603a1
messages.subject: comments on gtable
parts:
Hi

Simon Potter and I did some digging in 'gtable' (to get the new 'ggplot2' plots to export properly with 'gridSVG') and we found a few things we'd like to comment on ...

- a request:  could 'gtable' please export a gtable_grob() function or somesuch that creates a gTree from a gtable (most of the current body of grd.draw.gtable()) ?

- a suggestion:  grid.draw.gtable() currently creates an object with class of either "gtableParent" or c("gtableParent", "gtableChild").  The former has just a preDrawDetails() method (to push its 'layoutvp'), but the latter has a grid.draw() method (to push its 'wrapvp' first), which is a bit awkward.  If the latter class was instead c("gtableChild", "gtableParent"), then you could have a preDrawDetails.gtableParent() method to push the 'layoutvp' and  a preDrawDetails.gtableChild() method to push the 'wrapvp' then just NextMethod().  (?)

(first post to a Google Group so apologies for any etiquette breaking)

Paul

messages.subject: Re: comments on gtable
parts: Hi Paul,

Simon Potter and I did some digging in 'gtable' (to get the new 'ggplot2' plots to export properly with 'gridSVG') and we found a few things we'd like to comment on ...

- a request:  could 'gtable' please export a gtable_grob() function or somesuch that creates a gTree from a gtable (most of the current body of grd.draw.gtable()) ?


 
- a suggestion:  grid.draw.gtable() currently creates an object with class of either "gtableParent" or c("gtableParent", "gtableChild").  The former has just a preDrawDetails() method (to push its 'layoutvp'), but the latter has a grid.draw() method (to push its 'wrapvp' first), which is a bit awkward.  If the latter class was instead c("gtableChild", "gtableParent"), then you could have a preDrawDetails.gtableParent() method to push the 'layoutvp' and  a preDrawDetails.gtableChild() method to push the 'wrapvp' then just NextMethod().  (?)

IIRC, the reason is as followings.
drawGTree() first tris to push the vp of gTree by calling pushvpgp(x) and then call preDrawDetails(x).
But in some cases, e.g., the nested gtable, the wrapvp need to be pushed before the pushvpgp(x) is called.

kohske

Paul - What would be the purpose of returning a gTree? I ask is because gTrees have nice methods for displaying all the children (grid.ls) and retrieving specific child objects (getGrob), but gtables don't. Presently, traversing a gtable hierarchy is complicated. This is a part of gtable that could use improvement and it would be nice to get some input on how best to do that.

-Winston

messages.author: 224a7d15b7a603a1
messages.subject: Re: comments on gtable
parts:
The motivation is mostly selfish;  to get 'gridSVG' to work with "gtable" objects, we need to replicate what happens when a "gtable" object is drawn (because it does not draw in the standard way).  That effectively means we have to replicate the actions of grid.draw() and drawDetails() and preDrawDetails() methods.  We can do this by inspecting the 'gtable' code, which is nasty, but it would be a bit less nasty if we could do at least some of the replication by calling 'gtable' functions.  Specifically, if there was a function, say gtable.grob(), that grid.draw.gtable() called to create a gTree then we could more easily replicate the actions of grid.draw.gtable() by also calling gtable.grob().  Does that make sense?

This problem does also echo a wider issue, which you have alluded to, which is how to access the components of a grob (or gTree) that only creates its components at drawing time (grid.xaxis() is a good example).  The current solutions are (i) give up (ii) provide access via gEdit() and friends (see the 'edits' argument to grid.xaxis()), but I have wondered about a third way that allows a grob (or gTree) to be "flattened" so that it is actually replaced by its components on the grid display list when it draws.  I haven't thought through a proper design of this idea, but it might involve breaking the current drawDetails() approach into separate build-something-to-draw step followed by a drawing-it step (which is sort of what I am suggesting with the gtable.grob() function request).

Paul
